value.rationale: In a bistable higher-order contagion model, choosing which agents initially carry the same average infection can reverse extinction versus endemicity. The sharp recovery boundary 7/25 identifies where variance ceases to predict local seeding direction; a precisely defined third-moment/skewness sign takes over even for seed vectors with equal mean and variance. The minimal three-node triangle makes this a natural base motif rather than an arbitrary sample or routine parameter substitution. The analytic threshold surface is meaningful for the deterministic seeding problem even without broader networks.
